wstep: This card describes the NCHFP recipe for apricot jam without added pectin: crushed, peeled apricots cooked with lemon juice and sugar until thick and processed in a boiling-water bath.

ostrzezenia.tekst: Apricot pH varies: the US FDA list gives 3.30–4.80, so the upper end is above 4.6, the limit for acid foods. This recipe is tested with lemon juice: do not leave it out or reduce it, and do not reduce the sugar.

akapity: NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml.
For about 10 half-pint jars NCHFP uses 2 quarts (about 1.9 l) of crushed, peeled apricots, 1/4 cup of lemon juice and 6 cups of sugar.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): use bottled lemon juice in the amount given; NCHFP notes that fresh lemon juice can vary in acidity.
NCHFP warns not to reduce the sugar in traditional recipes: too little sugar prevents gelling and may allow yeasts and molds to grow.
Sterilize the jars.
NCHFP puts the empty jars right side up on the rack in a boiling-water canner and fills the canner and jars with hot (not boiling) water to 1 inch (about 2.5 cm) above the tops of the jars.
To sterilize empty jars, NCHFP boils them for 10 minutes below 1000 ft, and above that 1 minute longer for each additional thousand feet.
JarAtlas rule for metres: boil the jars for 10 minutes up to 300 m, and add 1 minute for every further 300 m or part of it.
To peel apricots, NCHFP dips the washed fruit in boiling water for 30–60 seconds until the skins loosen, dips it quickly in cold water and slips off the skins.
Combine all the ingredients and bring slowly to a boil, stirring occasionally until the sugar dissolves.
Cook rapidly until thick, about 25 minutes; as the mixture thickens, stir often so it does not stick.
Remove from the heat.
Just before filling, remove and drain the hot sterilized jars one at a time.
Fill the hot jam into hot, sterile jars, leaving 1/4 inch (about 0.6 cm) of headspace.
Wipe the jar rims with a damp clean paper towel, put on two-piece metal lids and process in a boiling-water canner.
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process half-pint and pint jars for 5 minutes.
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased.
At 1001–6000 ft (above 300 m up to 1800 m) process them for 10 minutes.
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process them for 15 minutes.
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m.
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage.
The NCHFP table gives times only for half-pint and pint jars.
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): a pint holds about 473 ml, so a 0.5 l jar has no tested time in this recipe; use jars of up to 473 ml.
Keep opened jam in the refrigerator at 40 °F (about 4 °C) or lower.
Regular full-sugar cooked jams like this one are best kept in the refrigerator for 1 month after opening.
Discard jam with mold on it; USDA and microbiologists advise against scooping out the mold and eating the rest.
